newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine police despair of solving newsman's murder.
newsitem.headline: Argentine police despair of solving newsman's murder.

text.p: Argentine police probing the murder of a news photographer in January are beginning to doubt they will ever discover who ordered it, the man heading the investigation said in comments published on Thursday.
"It's almost impossible to get to the intellectual author of this crime," Inspector Victor Fogelman told local media.

The murder of Jose Luis Cabezas, who worked for the weekly magazine Noticias, outraged the public and sparked mass protests. The newsman was handcuffed, beaten and shot in the head at a beach resort and his body burned beyond recognition.

Police have arrested one of their colleagues and a gang of small-time crooks working with him for the killing itself, but suspect it was ordered by someone much more powerful and have named businessman Alfredo Yabran as their prime suspect.

Fogelman said a month ago he believed he had "a good chance" of solving the crime and was "knocking on Alfredo Yabran's door." Yabran has been linked to the murder by phone calls made by the arrested policeman, and because Cabezas had published rare photos of the notoriously camera-shy tycoon.
But Yabran, also accused by the opposition of heading a mafia with powerful friends in the Peronist government, denies any link with the crime and has not been charged by any court.

Eduardo Duhalde, the high-profile Peronist governor of Buenos Aires province where Cabezas was killed, has staked much political capital on solving the crime and pledged on Wednesday he would "not let the case be forgotten."

Duhalde's security chief Carlos Brown tried on Thursday to offset Fogelman's comments, telling reporters: "The case continues at full pace, we are not stopping and in recent days there have been important advances."
